To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
during cadmium-induced malignant cell transformation, DNMT1 inhibition reverses the hypermethylation of the RASSF1a and p16 tumor suppressor genes.

during chronic cadmium-induced malignant prostate transformation, DNMT3b up-regulation precedes and is necessary for the development of genomic DNA hypermethyltion and tumor suppressor gene silencing, which are key events in the development of human cancer.
chronic exposure to cadmium induces malignant transformation in human prostate cells that is associated with increased expression of DNMT3B and generalized DNA hypermethlation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cadmium in human prostate carcinogenesis.
the role of cadmium and its metabolite, cadmium-protein complexes, in the development of prostate cancer.
the mechanisms by which cadmium induces malignant transformation of human prostate epithelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic cadmium exposure causes malignant transformation of human prostate cells by inducing overexpression of DNMT3a/b, which causes generalized DNA hypermethilation.
chronic cadmium exposure induces malignant transformation of human prostate epithelial cells through a mechanism that involves increased de novo DNA methylation.
cadmium exposure causes overexpression of DNMT3B, resulting in generalized hypermethylation and inactivation of tumor suppressor genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pattern of genomic hyper-methylation that occurs during cadmium-induced malignant tranformation is unique and is correlated with over-expression of the de novo DNA methyltransferase DNMT3b.

the cadmium-transformed human prostate cell line (CTPE) has increased de novo DNA methyltransferase 3b (DNMT3b), increased DNMT enzymic activity and hypermethylation of CpG islands in the promoter region of the tumor suppressors RASSF1 and p16, resulting in silencing of these genes.
cadmium exposure induces overexpression of DNMT3a/b, resulting in generalized DNA hyper-methylation and gene silenc-ing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cadmium induces malignant transformation of prostate cells by a unique mechanism that involves overexpression of DNMT3B.
DNMT3a and 3b can be induced in human cells to cause hypermethylation and that this is a mechanism that is important in carcinogenesis.
cadmium-induced DNA hypermethylation is associated with increased expression of DNMT3B and is not due to decreased expression of DNMT1.
